request: 超大 Markdown 文档（至少 100 MiB）包含内嵌图片和附件时支持导出 PDF；附件随 PDF 一并打包，并允许从 PDF 点击链接下载附件。
acceptance: Markdown PDF export accepts and completes documents of at least 100 MiB without asking users to split solely because of Markdown text length or DOM node count; mixed text, tables, code, diagrams, images and local attachments remain represented.

Directly referenced local attachments are embedded in the generated PDF, listed in a clear appendix, and exposed as clickable PDF links that open/save the corresponding embedded file; external URLs are kept external and never fetched as local files.
Attachment names and paths are sanitized, duplicate references are embedded once, and output remains a single downloadable PDF with no workspace sidecar files.

Existing cancellation, lock, source identity, image/resource failure, PDF layout, and progress behaviors remain intact; resource-specific limits are explicit and do not impose the old 32 MiB cap on the Markdown text itself.

requirements.summary: User requires PDF export for Markdown documents at least 100 MiB that contain mixed embedded images and linked files, and wants referenced attachments bundled inside the PDF with clickable download/open links. Keep it a single PDF download and do not require manual splitting.
evidence: Observed existing PDF export is browser-side and paginated; `validateDOM` rejects over 50,000 nodes, image rendering totals are capped at 32 MiB, and ZIP resource export has 64-item/32-MiB limits. Existing PDF does not embed attachments.

design.summary: For PDF, split the source at bounded line/block boundaries (preserving/reopening fenced code and repeating reference definitions/table headers when a boundary falls inside them), render and paginate each bounded fragment into one jsPDF document, then discard its DOM before continuing. Keep page canvas and per-chunk image budgets. Embed unique local reference blobs as PDF EmbeddedFile/Filespec objects in the catalog and render an attachment appendix with native clickable FileAttachment annotations; retain external links unchanged. This avoids enlarging the editor, backend, or unrelated ZIP resource limit.
evidence: Local text file content is already resident in the Markdown editor; incremental parsing prevents a second full-document HTML DOM.
jsPDF 4.2.1 putPage/putCatalog events and EmbeddedFile/Filespec objects are used to associate native GoToE annotations with the embedded attachment catalog.

implementation.summary: PDF export now splits Markdown into approximately 192 Ki-character fragments and appends all fragment pages to one jsPDF. Directly linked local non-image files are deduplicated, path-resolved and sanitized, embedded in the PDF catalog with GoToE link annotations in a final appendix. External URLs stay untouched. Image bytes remain globally capped at 32 MiB; embedded files are capped at 64 MiB each, 256 items and 256 MiB aggregate.
evidence: internal/server/web/app.js: Markdown rendering is lazy per PDF fragment
